steps: A presenter e-mails the shared inbox.
The coordinator reads it on Monday.
The coordinator updates the slot board.
problems: Last month a breakfast slot went to a presenter not trained on the desk, and the station was silent for twenty minutes.
Swaps sent after Monday are not seen until the next week.
cites: [A:A01 "last month a breakfast slot went to a presenter not trained on the desk, and the station was silent for twenty minutes"]

in: A checked list of swaps out.
cites: [A:A01 "Out: new presenter training, programme ideas, the outside broadcast rota."]

inputs.format: plain text, one swap per message

samples.description: A made-up week of swap messages.

cites: [S:S01 §whole file]
[S:S02 §whole file]

glossary.meaning: Signed off on running the studio desk alone.

acceptance_tests.words: I give it a month of made-up swap e-mails, and no slot ever goes to someone who isn't desk trained.

ranks.what: Reference documents in the context pack
Official documentation on the maker's own site

confidence.high: The row quotes the swap message and the training list entry that decided it.
confidence.medium: A reputable secondary source; not expected here.
confidence.low: Inferred or one weak source; such a swap is refused and raised as a question.

conflicts: The higher rank wins within its own area.
A conflict the ranks do not settle is reported with both citations, never decided silently.

output.description: One row per swap message, with a decision: approve or refuse. A swap that names no slot is refused as incomplete. A swap for the outside broadcast rota is refused as out of scope.
output.format: Table, one row per swap message
